newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes weaken on fundamental worries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes weaken on fundamental worries.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices weakened Wednesday, moving lower on fundamental concerns resulting from inventory data showing stock builds and extremely high utilization rates.
Both American Petroleum Institute and Departent of Energy statistics showed crude building substantially, with utilization rates from 98 percent to more than 100 percent.

Cash traders said there were of course two ways to look at the data. The bearish mindest focuses on the large amounts of crude sitting in storage, while the bulls look at the refinery runs as a sure sign of active demand.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing finished nearly 10 cents lower at $20.25-35 a barrel, working off a 15 cents advantage over the NYMEX futures prices due to firm Exchange for Physicals (EFPs).

Traders said EFP values may move out further in the next few days to around 20 cents, reflecting refiner worries about getting stuck with foreign barrels when delivery takes place for July NYMEX contracts.
"I think a lot more volume has been getting done in the EFP market. I don't if people have found a new religion or what," said a cash dealer.
On the grade front, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was stuck at a 16 cents discount to the marker all session, while Midland/WTI also steadied at 40-37 cents under WTI.
West Texas Sour/Midland sold between a $1.56-$1.60 discount, while Postings moved at $1.93-95.
Iraqi crude oil will remain in the market following Wednesday's decision by the U.N. Security Council to extend the "oil-for-food" accord another 180 days, starting June 8.
Despite reservations from the U.S. and British delegations, the humanitarian exception to broad sanctions against Iraq was allowed to continue at the present $2 billion sales limit.
